question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

The COVID-19 pandemic led to trade disruptions worldwide, but the agricultural and food sector __prove to more resilient__ than other sectors of the economy.
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The original sentence contains a tense-related error in the phrase "**prove to more resilient**."
 
• Since the sentence refers to a completed action in the past (during the COVID-19 pandemic), the correct tense should be the past tense "**proved**."
 
• The correct phrase is "**proved to be more resilient**," which aligns with the past context of the sentence.
 
• Thus, the correct option is **Option 4**, as it ensures both grammatical correctness and appropriate verb tense usage.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The COVID-19 pandemic led to trade disruptions worldwide, but the agricultural and food sector **proved to be more resilient** than other sectors of the economy."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "prove to be more resilient" **– This is incorrect because "prove" is in the present tense, which does not align with the past context of the sentence.
 
• **Option 2: "proved to been more resilient" **– This is incorrect because "been" is unnecessary and grammatically incorrect in this context.
 
• **Option 3: "proving to be more resilient" **– This is incorrect because "proving" is in the present continuous tense, which does not fit the past context of the sentence.
